questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
One of the most important factors for me was studying in an English-speaking country. I also wanted a destination that combined vibrant city life with easy access to beautiful nature, and Australia was the perfect fit.

Studying in an English-speaking country gives you access to a wide range of courses and makes it much easier to communicate with classmates, lecturers, and local people. This helps you settle in quickly, build friendships, and get the most out of both your academic and social experience. Living in Australia is also a great opportunity to improve your english.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Overall, I am very happy with my study abroad experience. The university offered a wide selection of subjects, which made it easy to find courses that matched my interests. The Orientation Week (O-Week) was also a great opportunity to meet other exchange and local students before the semester began.

I do have some reasons why my stay was not a 10/10. In general, the teaching was of a high quality. However, a few lecturers had very strong accents, which sometimes made it difficult to follow the lectures. Furthermore, I think the university could have done more to introduce us to people from the same academic program, but they do have an app where you can connect with people and arrange plans.

Apart from that, outside of university, I had an amazing experience. Melbourne is a fantastic city for students, with plenty of cultural events, cafés, restaurants, and activities. It is also an excellent base for exploring Australia and nearby destinations such as Tasmania, Sydney, and New Zealand, making it easy to combine studying with travel.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Most of the information you need is available through the university's Learning Management System (LMS). The university provides clear checklists and step-by-step guidance, making it easy to know what needs to be done and when. Overall, I found the information well organized and easy to access.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Before and after my arrival, I received several emails explaining the practical steps I needed to complete. The university also provided useful information during the orientation sessions in O-Week.

I did experience some issues with my course planning because two of my subjects had overlapping timetables. However, this was quickly resolved after speaking with the staff at Stop 1, who were very helpful and guided me through the available options.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Overall, I was very satisfied with the orientation and support provided by the university. The only reason I did not give the highest rating was that I found the process of dealing with overlapping subjects a little confusing at first. However, after contacting Stop 1, the issue was resolved quickly, and the staff were very helpful throughout the process.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Students at the university can apply for university-managed accommodation before arriving. I chose to stay at The Lofts, which is reserved for master's students and above. The application process was straightforward and completed online, although there was an application fee.

I applied a few weeks after applications had opened and was still offered a room, so there seems to be some flexibility. The Lofts is located directly across the street from campus, which made it extremely convenient for attending classes and participating in university activities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was almost living on campus, so I dont have a lot of advice. I found it very convenient to live close to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Overall, I was very happy with my accommodation. The location was excellent. Just across the street from the university and close to great cafés, Yo-Chi, and the beautiful Carlton Gardens. The Lofts also organized social activities during the first weeks, which made it easier to meet new people. I found some of my best friends through The Lofts. In addition, the facilities were excellent, including a gym, rooftop terrace and study rooms.

I also appreciated living with other master's students, as I felt most of us had similar lifestyles. My only drawbacks were that the accommodation was relatively expensive and that most of my flatmates were full-degree students rather than exchange students. If I were applying again, I would request to be placed with other exchange students in the comments section of the application, as I think that would have made it even easier to build a social network early on.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process was well organized and communicated through email and the university's online systems.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always ask for help from stop 1.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Overall, I was successful in registering for the classes I wanted to take. Some of the subjects I was interested in had prerequisite requirements, so I had to contact the subject coordinators to request permission to enroll. The coordinators were helpful, and in the end I was able to take the subjects I found most interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The registration process can take some time, as there are several steps to complete. My advice would be to start early and take the process one step at a time. Do not hesitate to contact the university or the relevant subject coordinator if you have any questions. Although the process may feel a little overwhelming at first, it is manageable, and the exchange experience is definitely worth the effort.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall, I was very satisfied with the academic programme. The courses were interesting, well structured, and academically rewarding. One challenge I experienced was that a few lecturers had very strong accents (from outside australia), which sometimes made it difficult to follow the lectures. This was not only my experience. Some of my Australian classmates mentioned that they also found certain lectures difficult to understand.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the BA class to be easy, while the two MA public health classes were comparable in difficulty and academic expectations to similar courses at the University of Copenhagen. The one MA class I took at another faculty was more challenging and required a greater workload and a different way of thinking.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Compared with the University of Copenhagen, I found that the style of teaching was different rather than more demanding. There was generally less required reading, but in several subjects students were expected to watch recorded lectures before attending class.

The structure of tutorials also varied between subjects. Some focused on answering questions about the course material, while others involved solving new exercises or provided time to work on assignments with guidance from the tutor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Database Systems & Data Modelling (INFO90002), Genetic Epidemiology (POPH90111), Australian Surfing (UNIB10028) and Infectious Disease Epidemiology (POPH90112).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend the Epidemiology courses, as I found them both interesting, relevant, and well structured. In particular, I recommend attending the online tutorials in the Genetic Epidemiology course. The tutor explained the material very clearly, making it easier to understand.

The Australian Surfing course was also a lot of fun and offered a unique Australian experience. However, future students should be aware that the course only includes one actual surfing session, with the remaining classes focusing on theory and related topics.

The final course I took was very interesting and academically rewarding, and I learned a great deal from it. However, the final exam was very challenging and included a hurdle requirement. In addition, the exam was scheduled quite late in June, which meant that I spent much of my final weeks in Melbourne studying instead of traveling and enjoying the city. For that reason, I would encourage future exchange students to consider whether this course fits with their plans for the end of the semester.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: One unexpected cost was the application fee for university accommodation, which was approximately DKK 400.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The Australian student visa and health insurance was pretty expensive. I found that good-quality coffee and eating out were generally a little cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not formally join any clubs, but the University of Melbourne offered a very wide range of clubs and societies, so there were plenty of opportunities to get involved. I attended a few classes with the FLARE dance club without becoming a member, and I found them very enjoyable.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The University of Melbourne offers a wide variety of cultural, athletic, and social activities for students. There are numerous clubs and societies covering everything from sports and dance to academic and cultural interests. The university also offers free fitness classes each week, and students have access to the swimming facilities during designated free hours.

In addition, the university has a dedicated exchange student club, which organizes social events and provides a great opportunity to meet other exchange students and build a network early in the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend participating in O-Week, as it is one of the best opportunities to meet new people and build friendships before the semester begins.

I also really enjoyed attending dance classes with the FLARE dance club, yoga classes offered through the university fitness program, and art events organized by the Graduate Student Association (GSA).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend traveling as much as your budget and schedule allow. Some highlights of my exchange was visiting Tasmania, New Zealand, Great ocean road, Sydney and Whitsundays. My personal strategy was to enjoy Melbourne during the summer at the beginning of the semester and then travel south before making my way north as the weather became cooler. This allowed me to experience the best weather in each destination throughout the semester. Finally, don't overlook the areas around Melbourne. Day or weekend trips to Brighton beach, the Mornington Peninsula and Grampians National Park are definitely worth it if you enjoy nature and beautiful scenery.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to adjust to life in Australia because, in many ways, the culture is similar to Denmark. People are friendly, speak English, and the lifestyle is relaxed, making it easy to settle in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I became friends with some Australian students through group work at university. Something as simple as suggesting that we have lunch together after class was the start of our friendship.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any major cultural challenges. The biggest adjustment was living with people from many different cultural backgrounds, as everyone had different daily routines, expectations, and standards regarding shared spaces and cleanliness.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: What I appreciated most was the openness and friendliness of the Australian culture. People were generally very approachable, relaxed, and welcoming. It was not uncommon for strangers to start a conversation, which made it much easier to feel included and accepted as a newcomer. I also appreciated the more laid-back attitude to everyday life, which created a positive and friendly atmosphere both on and off campus.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Participate in O-Week and other social activities from the beginning. It is by far the easiest way to meet both exchange and local students, and many of the friendships you make during the first week will last throughout your exchange.
2. Travel whenever you have the opportunity. Melbourne is an excellent base for exploring Australia. I highly recommend visiting places such as Tasmania, the Great Ocean Road, Whitsundays, Sydney, and, if your budget allows, New Zealand.
3. Apply for scholarships and save more money than you think you will need. Although it is possible to live on a budget, there are so many amazing opportunities to travel and experience Australia that the costs quickly add up.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: My biggest piece of advice is to make the most of every opportunity. Say yes to social events, weekend trips, and activities, even if they are outside your comfort zone. Some of my best memories came from experiences I had not originally planned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the people I met along the way. I made friends with students from many different countries and cultural backgrounds, which gave me new perspectives and memories. Another rewarding aspect was becoming much more confident in speaking English through everyday conversations, university life, and traveling.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was the first few weeks, when everything was new. Getting familiar with the university systems, understanding the course structure, and building a new social network all happened at the same time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: The exam timetable for Semester 1 is released relatively late (around mMay). If you prefer to book your return flight well in advance, it is worth considering this when selecting your subjects, as courses with in-person final exams may limit your flexibility.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
